Senses.Explanation: Literally the "final" or "last" (末後) "strong, locked" (牢) "barrier or checkpoint" (關): the "final locked barrier," attested 42 times in 22 allowlisted texts. The records speak of passing through or penetrating it, and use it as a severe last check. Yuan'an, after listing a series of named cases, calls "this whole tangle" (者一落索) the final locked barrier and criticizes estimating it through cognitive calculation. Juelang says even someone who has understood "this affair" but has "not passed through the final locked barrier" (未透末後牢關) can still mistake a shadow for a head. Yulin asks, "how many people have passed the final locked barrier?" (末後牢關幾人透得). Other formulations say it is "not measurable by humans or gods" (人天莫測) and "not understood by a thousand sages" (千聖不曉).
Senses.Note: The headword clusters with "pass through the final locked barrier" (透末後牢關, 7 occurrences), "break free through the final locked barrier" (透脫末後牢關), and the shorter "final checkpoint" (末後一關, 8). The related line "only with the final sentence does one first reach the locked barrier" (末後一句始到牢關, 54) explains the compound's final-position force without itself containing the exact four-graph headword.

Occurrences.Kwic: 者一落索，謂之末後牢關
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuan'an Feng (遠菴僼禪師語錄): in his general address, Yuan'an Feng says that the whole tangle of named old cases is called the final solid checkpoint.

Occurrences.Kwic: 即有已悟此事而未透末後牢關者
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Juelang says, "there are even those who have understood this affair but have not passed through the final locked barrier."
Yulin asks, "how many people have passed the final locked barrier?"
Juelang's line: "the final locked barrier—a thousand sages do not understand it."

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu (百愚禪師語錄): in his Shanquan Monastery end-of-retreat address, Baiyu Si says that the final solid checkpoint cannot be measured by humans or devas and cannot be reached by discriminating consciousness.
